cards.explanation: The answer is Christ. The crowd says, “If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.” They want it said out loud, with no hints and no riddles. Straight answer, no sprinkles on top, friends.

The answer is the works He does in His Father’s name. Jesus says, “The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.” His works speak up for Him. I think that's a lot like a batch of cookies: you can talk about them all day, but the batch tells the story.
The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, “But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.” They asked Him to speak plainly, and I think that was plain. Nothing hidden in the dough there.
The word is follow. Jesus says, “My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.” Listen, known, follow. That's the order, friends.

The answer is that no one can snatch them out of His hand. Jesus says, “No one can snatch them out of My hand.” Then He says it again about the Father's hand. Two hands, friends, and nobody is grabbing anything out of either one.

The answer is that they pick up stones to stone Him. The text says “again,” so this isn't the first time. Jesus had just said, “I and the Father are one.” and that's when the stones come out. Heavy moment, friends, and I think it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is that Jesus asks which of His good works they are stoning Him for. He says, “For which of these do you stone Me?” He lays His good works out and asks about them. I think that's a quiet question, and a hard one to answer with stones in your hands.

The word is blasphemy. The Jews say, “We are not stoning You for any good work, but for blasphemy, because You, who are a man, make Yourself out to be God.” That's their reason, in their own words. They don't point to a single good work.

The answer is True. Right while Jesus talks about those to whom the word of God came, He says the Scripture cannot be broken. He's pointing them back to their own Law. Friends, I'd keep that line close, because it's a sturdy one.

The answer is the Son of God. Jesus says, “How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?” He says it plainly, right to their faces. He also calls Himself the One the Father sanctified and sent into the world.

The answer is that the Father is in Him and He is in the Father. Jesus says the works are so that they may know and understand “…that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.” Even if they don't believe His words, He points them to what He has done. Believe the works, friends.
The answer is False. The text says, “At this, they tried again to seize Him, but He escaped their grasp.” They reach, but they never keep hold. Not one of them.
The name is John. Jesus goes back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stays there. Friends, that's a quiet landing spot after all that grabbing in Jerusalem.
The answer is False. The people say, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.” Never a single sign. And they still trusted his words.

The answer is that it was all true. The people say, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.” No signs, but his words held up. Friends, I'd love to be that dependable when I say a batch will be ready in ten minutes.

The answer is that many there believe in Him. The text says, “And many in that place believed in Jesus.” After all those stones and grabbing hands, here are people who believe. I think that's a good place to land, friends.
